messages:
ashley: Quick sync 5m. Proposed focus: service credential introspection API + RBAC cache invalidation semantics. Need to settle strong/weak guarantees before RFC.
maria: +1. We keep hearing incidents where role revokes aren't reflected for minutes. Prod needs bounded staleness.
jamal: Two modes I can see: (A) Strong: every request triggers introspection to authz service (accurate, higher latency). (B) Cached: token includes role claims + TTL and edges validate only ttl + optional revocation set (fast, eventual). Which do we standardize?
sebastian: hybrid: default cached tokens (claim TTL short, e.g., 5m) + an optional "force-check" header for admin flows that must hit introspect. For emergency revokes, push revocation ids to edge caches.
nina: Implementation question: what is the token shape? If token is opaque, introspection makes sense. If token is JWT-like with embedded role claims we can avoid per-request calls. But JWTs risk replay if roles change.
maria: prefer opaque tokens from a security standpoint. We can embed a compact claim-snapshot in the token metadata (signed by broker) to allow fast path without full introspect, and still require edges to check revocation feed.
jamal: That puts complexity in token verification. What about adding a volatile claim-version header: token carries claim_version=X, edges check local claim_version map -> if local == X accept, else call introspect. That keeps common fast path and bounds introspect rate.
sebastian: claim-version map fits well with our rollout. We can push claim_version updates atomically per-actor on role changes. Need to size the map and eviction policy though.
nina: SDKs need a transparent auto-refresh if introspect fails with stale cache. Also add metrics: introspect_calls_per_1000, cache_hit_rate, avg_introspect_latency.
maria: Revocation: two vectors  immediate hard revoke (security incident) and policy revoke (role changes). For immediate we must ensure edge denies active tokens within ~10s. For policy revoke we can accept eventual convergence (<=5m).
jamal: To get ~10s we need push-based revocation invalidation to edge nodes. Options: streaming RPC (grpc stream) or pubsub delta pushes. Streaming is lower-latency.
sebastian: streaming RPC with lightweight revocation ids + small bloom filter update is my pick. We need to benchmark memory on edge fleet.
nina: Also consider degraded mode: if streaming breaks, edges fallback to cached claim_version checks and periodically poll the authz service. Document fallback in runbook.
maria: RBAC evaluation frequency  do we evaluate at token mint or at introspection? I vote mint-only for performance: mint-time eval produces claim snapshot. Introspection returns the current snapshot if asked.
jamal: Mint-only means rotation + revocation needed for mid-lease changes. Make default lease TTL short (5m) and allow pinned leases for long-running daemon jobs with an attestation handshake.
sebastian: Attestation: require a signed job-runner identity from the orchestration layer for pins. Keep operator approval process in UI and audit-bot.
nina: Cross-project calls: if a token minted in project-A calls service-B, do we honor project-A role claims or require service-B to re-evaluate against its own bindings?
mamaria: (typo) Whoops. We should require the receiving service to map incoming actor to a local service-actor identity via a trust mapping. That prevents privilege escalation across org boundaries.
maria: Concrete: token includes origin_project and actor_id. Receiver checks trust mapping table; if trusted, it maps to a local actor alias and uses its RBAC. If not trusted, reject or require least-privileged default.
jamal: Mapping tables need lifecycle management. They should be explicit, declare allowed outbound actors, and rotate keys used for attestation. Audit logs must record mapping resolution.
sebastian: Operational concerns: what happens when authz service is unavailable? Edge must fail safe to deny sensitive endpoints and allow read-only weaker flows. Document policy levels: critical, protected, public.
nina: Testing matrix: 1) mint+introspect latencies 2) revocation push p99 propagation 3) cache reconciliation after stream drop 4) cross-project mapping correctness.
mamaria: oops again.
maria: I'll clean up typos. Next steps: I will draft the RFC with the following recommended defaults: opaque tokens + claim_version fast-path, default lease TTL 5m, pinned leases for operator/daemon with attestation, streaming revocation for hard revokes, introspect endpoint for edge fallback, mapping table for cross-project calls, and clear runbook for degraded mode.
jamal: Add a staging playbook for power-surge (authz service overloaded) and quota throttles per-tenant for mint calls.
sebastian: I'll prototype the bloom-filter revocation stage and measure memory+cpu.
nina: I'll update SDK RFC section for auto-refresh and expose introspect helpers.
ops-bot: Reminder: schedule security review and include incident playbook steps.
audit-bot: Audit note: ensure all mapping table changes produce immutable audit entries and require two-step approval for cross-project mappings.
ashley: tiny: put a TTL cap on pinned leases (e.g., 72h) and require re-attestation for extensions.
maria: agreed. I'll include that. I'll post RFC draft link once ready. Thanks, team."
